title: A closed subgroup of a connected affine group is detected by its identity stalk
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $j:K\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $e_G$ and $e_K$ for their identity $k$-points, and $\mathcal O_{G,e_G}$ and $\mathcal O_{K,e_K}$ for the stalks of their structure sheaves at these points. If the homomorphism of local $k$-algebras $j^\sharp_{e_K}:\mathcal O_{G,e_G}\to\mathcal O_{K,e_K}$ induced by $j$ is an isomorphism, then $j$ is an isomorphism of $k$-group schemes. Neither $G$ nor $K$ is assumed reduced or smooth; the characteristic of $k$ is arbitrary.

source.place: Agent-formulated identity-stalk consequence of the translation argument in 1.8 (printed p.9), with finite-type rational closed points used as in the homogeneity discussion of Chapter 1. This precise scheme-theoretic criterion is not asserted to be a numbered theorem of Milne; its full intended proof is in report.md. No single Stacks tag supplies the criterion.

proof.text: Choose $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Apply the affine-pair criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the structure morphism and the pair $(G,\operatorname{Spec}k)$: $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Thus $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes $K=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $j$ as the quotient map. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose a finite list of ideal generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ for $I$ (the list may be empty).

source.place: Tags 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); Noetherian algebra input as in lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components; Tag 00FM (section-Noetherian).

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be the prime of $e_G$. Each $a_i$ maps to zero on $K$, so its germ at $e_G$ maps to zero under $j^\sharp_{e_K}$; this is restriction compatibility in [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. The assumed injectivity makes that germ zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) with the affine open $G$: there is $s_i\in A\setminus\mathfrak m$ with $s_i a_i=0$. Put $s=\prod_i s_i$, with empty product $1$. Then $s\notin\mathfrak m$ and $sI=0$, since $s$ kills every generator. In particular $I A_s=0$. This uses vanishing in local rings, not vanishing in residue fields.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), local-ring description; finite denominator argument applied to the finite list from step 1.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $U=D(s)$ is an affine open containing $e_G$, with coordinate ring $A_s$. Its inverse image in $K$ is $D(\bar s)$ with coordinate ring $(A/I)_{\bar s}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute], this is $A_s/I A_s=A_s$, and the induced homomorphism is the quotient homomorphism with zero kernel. Thus $j^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism, using the contravariant affine description [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $t:U\to K$ be its inverse followed by $j^{-1}(U)\hookrightarrow K$; then $jt$ is the inclusion $U\hookrightarrow G$.

For $h\in K(k)$, write $g=j(h)$. Use the translations of [def-sc-group-scheme-translate] and their inverses in [lem-sc-translation-automorphism], for both $G$ and $K$. Because $j$ is a group homomorphism, $jL_h^K=L_g^G j$. Consequently $L_h^K t(L_{g^{-1}}^G|_{gU}):gU\to K$ is a section of $j$ over the open $gU=L_g^G(U)$. It is the inverse to $j^{-1}(gU)\to gU$: the reverse composite is the identity because $j$ is injective on functor-of-points sets by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Equivalently the two translations identify this restriction with the restriction over $U$ in step 3. In particular $gU\subseteq |K|$, as a subset of $|G|$. Define the open subset $V=\bigcup_{h\in K(k)}j(h)U\subseteq |G|$. We have $V\subseteq |K|$ and $j$ is an isomorphism over every member of this union.

source.place: 1.8, printed p.9: translation isomorphisms; apply the group-homomorphism identity to the restriction in step 3.

proof.text: The subset $|K|\setminus V$ is closed in $G$, since $|K|$ is closed and $V$ is open. If nonempty, it contains a point $x$ closed in $G$ by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], applied to this closed subset of the finite-type scheme $G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], $\kappa(x)=k$ over $k$. The evaluation $A\to k$ therefore defines $g\in G(k)$ with underlying point $x$. Since $x\in |K|=V(I)$, this evaluation kills $I$ and factors through $A/I$, giving $h\in K(k)$ with $j(h)=g$. But $e_G\in U$ implies $x=g e_G\in gU\subseteq V$, a contradiction. Thus $V=|K|$. This subset is both open and closed, and contains $e_G$. Connectedness in [def-weil-connected-scheme] now gives $V=|G|$. Hence the opens $j(h)U$ from step 4 cover all of $G$.

For $a\in I$, the section of $\mathcal O_G$ represented by $a$ pulls back to zero on $K$. On every open $j(h)U$ in the cover of step 5 the restriction of $j$ is an isomorphism by step 4, so $a|_{j(h)U}=0$. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom gives $a=0$ globally: the structure sheaf and restriction-compatible homomorphisms are those of [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Thus $I=0$ and the quotient $A\to A/I$ is an isomorphism. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $j$ is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes. Its inverse preserves multiplication, identity and inverse: apply $j$ to each proposed compatibility equation and use the corresponding compatibility of the group homomorphism $j$, then cancel $j$ using its inverse. This proves the isomorphism of $k$-group schemes required by [def-sc-group-scheme].
